verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew successfully landed on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time" (R1); "The Orion capsule has splashed down in the Pacific Ocean... on April 10, 2026" (R2); "splashed down into the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday night" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm successful splashdown (referred to as landing) on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Floating in the Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego" (R1); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego" (R2); "Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state splashdown in Pacific Ocean off San Diego, California.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule arrived at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time" (R1); "The splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. ET" (R2); "touched down at 5.07pm (1.07am BST)" matching 8:07 EDT/5:07 PDT (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources give exact time of 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) for splashdown/arrival.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew were recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "hoisted them up... to the U.S.S. John P. Murtha" (R1); "flown to the flight deck of USS John P. Murtha" (R2); "recovery crew from the USS John P Murtha" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm recovery by USS John P. Murtha.

verifications.claim: The landing type was parachute-assisted splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "descending under parachutes... hitting the waters" (R1); "parachute-assisted splashdown" (R4); "three main parachutes deployed... splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe parachute deployment leading to splashdown in Pacific Ocean.

verifications.claim: The landing location was near San Diego, CA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "waters off San Diego" (R1); "off the coast of San Diego, California" (R2); "off the coast of San Diego" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources specify location near/off coast of San Diego, CA.

verifications.claim: The landing time was April 10, 2026, 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources match exact date and dual time zones for splashdown.

verifications.claim: The recovery ship was USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "U.S.S. John P. Murtha" (R1); "USS John P. Murtha" (R2); "USS John P Murtha" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently identified as recovery ship across all sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen" (R1); same crew listed in R2, R3, R4, etc.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names listed identically in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew completed a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources repeatedly describe as 10-day mission, despite precise duration slightly less.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew were the first humans to travel around the moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972" (R1); "first humans... since the crew of Apollo 17 in December 1972" (R3); "first human lunar mission in more than 50 years" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first since 1972 (over 50 years to 2026), traveling around the moon.
